T.8.notes: Targeted versus untargeted training of a learnable-strategy learner (TargetableMeta) with the same episode budget, improvement on held-out probes of the curriculum's target; sign-flip test; needs >= 3 distinct targets. Credit diagnosis (development probe seed 8777, 8 worlds per category x 11 arms, in-shell): ranking the arms by the learner's mean episode_gain across worlds matches the ranking by the evaluator's mean normalised score with Spearman 0.54-0.94 in 7 of 8 categories (0.21 in skill_combination); the selected arm's regret against the category's best arm is 0.006-0.26 (summed 0.48). Two scale-free alternatives (gain over the first tick relative to it; its signed log) lower the summed regret to 0.28-0.37 but are worse in other categories, and the per-category best arms differ from one another by little in five categories, so no credit change makes the targeted arm reliably better; not changed. T.8's design (T8_DESIGN) and failing result stand. Wave 3b repair 2 (development only, dev seed 900, not shipped): a contextual variant (one bandit per public context: lever count, horizon band, price lever) so that targeted training would concentrate experience where the weakness shows: on the lag-blind learner's target (delayed credit) targeted and untargeted training both improved the held-out probes by 0.15 - the coarse public contexts are shared with uniformly drawn worlds and the arm that is best on average also repairs the lag-blindness. Reverted; T.8 needs weakness-specific remedies that uniform training would not pick (a world-grammar/learner design question), not a different test. Development (dev seed 7300, 20 uniformly drawn generated worlds, common random numbers): the mean normalised score of TargetableMeta's 11 arms lies within 0.11-0.21 except the lag-blind arm (settle 0, one-tick measurements) at 0.35 (per-arm se about 0.1): the 'lag-blind' planted deficiency is the best strategy on uniformly drawn worlds, so uniform training has little reason to leave it and the strategy differences that targeted training could exploit are small next to probe noise; a T.8 redesign was not attempted in this pass.
T.8.status_claim: FAILS (unofficial gate run on the branch head, design fixed before the run): targeted vs untargeted improvement p 0.296 (20 pairs, mean +0.018, 9 better / 9 worse, 6 distinct targets). Diagnosis after the run (development, not a new test): the TargetableMeta learner's own credit (episode gain over its first tick) is nearly flat across its strategies in most generated categories (e.g. experimentation 0.38-0.43, while the evaluator's normalised score of the same strategies ranges -0.10 to 0.55), so targeted training cannot pick the strategy that is better on the evaluator's measure; it needs a learner whose own credit resolves strategies (a learner problem, not evidence that the worlds miss their weaknesses: T.5 shows the curriculum finds them)

T.4 (sequential design, D-69 addendum 3): static generated worlds cannot pass admission's no_dominant_strategy check by construction (the hindsight-best constant is optimal when the best setting does not move); wandering-optimum worlds pass only when the reference's tracking gain beats the hindsight simple policies (constant, threshold, win-stay/lose-shift, explore-then-commit, all built from the hindsight-best constants) by a quarter. With an uninformative default (DEF-N-8) the generator's yield of fully validated worlds is low (estimated 2-4%; dominance-check passes on development streams 5 of 48 and 2 of 24 wandering worlds), so T.4 walks the stream until 50 worlds validate (at most 1000 structures, about 3250 worlds). The yield is reported with the count: a pass shows that the pipeline produces validated worlds, at a measured cost, not that most generated worlds are admissible. The 2-3 / 7-8 centre bands are a generator regularity: an explore-then-commit rule over the two quartiles reaches a median 0.43 of the oracle's improvement on wandering worlds and 0.46 on 48 calibrated generated worlds (the calibration-shortcut threshold is 0.5).

T.5: forgetting and generalization are excluded from the selection test (a frozen learner has no truth there); the eight learners are frozen within-episode adapters, so T.5 tests selection among the eight template categories only.

SP-14.3: the curriculum's forgetting and generalization statistics are measured from revisits (10% review items); at 90 measured items generalization rests on about 8 seen-structure items over 3 structural categories, so it is noisy (pooled-variance 95% t margin; null false-positive rate about 3% in the unit test).

SP-15.5 / U.1 Level 5: the architecture-neutral ReferenceLearner (crucible.experience) is at the score floor on Tier 1 evaluation worlds whatever it was trained on, so the A/B/C/D comparison and Level 5 transfer are executable but uninformative (DEF-N-7, owner L/N).

The evaluator, fresh-process child and learner probes are process-isolated only: same uid and filesystem, no uid/Landlock jail. A learner with arbitrary file access could search the disk for the sealed salt; it never receives its location (CRUCIBLE_V5_SEALED_DIR is set only in the evaluator's environment).

Positive controls are lever-interface learners on rapid primitive-graph families (normalised scores need the evaluator-side lever oracle, which exists only for that engine). Families are chosen where each control's capability was established on independent seeds (instrument.establish); on families built to punish greedy adaptation (dl_*, mk_signal, ...) simple adapters lose, which is reported, not hidden.

Generated worlds (compose) are mostly static optimisations: the dominance check of rapid admission rejects most of them (T.4). Their 'participant populations' are equation primitives inside one causal graph.
Curriculum planted weaknesses mostly surface as delayed-credit deficits; distinct targets for T.8 are not guaranteed by construction and are measured.

Caches: establishment, control batteries and curves are cached under $CRUCIBLE_CACHE/research_v5 keyed by a digest of research/v5, rapid, mechanisms, domains and civ sources; any edit there recomputes them (minutes).
